yt_botcheck:
YouTube is blocking this address and wants proof of a real visitor ("Sign in to confirm you're not a bot").

Sign in to YouTube in a browser on the machine running the bot, then set in .env:
YT_COOKIES=chrome   (or edge, firefox, brave)
then restart the bot. It reads the cookies from that browser.

This is about the network address, not the bot. On a home connection it often clears on its own after a while; on a shared server it may not.
yt_dpapi:
The browser's cookies are sealed by Windows and this process cannot open them (DPAPI). It only works for the same Windows account that owns the browser profile.

Two ways around it:
1. Export a cookies.txt from the browser and point the bot at the file, which needs no decryption at all:
   install the "Get cookies.txt LOCALLY" extension, open youtube.com, click the extension, save the file, then in .env set
   YT_COOKIES=C:\tgsave\cookies.txt
2. Run the bot as the same Windows account as the browser, or set YT_COOKIES=firefox.
